title: Harden remote calendar redirects, secret replay, and body limits
description:
## Finding

Remote calendar sources bypass a safe shared HTTP policy and can redirect secrets or allocate an unbounded response before enforcing their advertised 32 MiB ceiling.

Both ICS URL and CalDAV construct a new default reqwest client for each fetch. The default redirect policy is enabled. CalDAV 307/308 redirects can replay the REPORT body, including the opaque sync token, to a redirect target; cross-origin header scrubbing does not protect secrets embedded in that body. Same-host redirects can retain Basic/Bearer authorization, and no policy forbids HTTPS-to-HTTP downgrade. Redirect targets are not constrained to the configured origin, scheme, or address class, creating a calendar-triggered SSRF path.

The nominal response cap is checked only after `.text().await` has buffered and decoded the full body. Content-Length is advisory and absent for chunked responses; compressed/chunked responses can exceed it after decoding. A malicious or compromised subscription endpoint can exhaust process memory. CalDAV does not even pre-check Content-Length. Error responses have no bounded diagnostic-body policy or content-type validation.

Rebuilding clients also discards connection pools and repeats DNS/TCP/TLS work every polling pass.

## Evidence at audited commit

* `crates/thegn-svc/src/calendar/ics_url.rs:19-20,83-101,127-140`: fresh default client; credentials attached before redirects; body limit enforced after `text()`.
* `crates/thegn-svc/src/calendar/caldav.rs:23-24,236-263,290-296`: the same policy gap; REPORT carries sync-token XML and has only a post-buffer limit.
* `crates/thegn-core/src/config_calendar.rs:264-272,392-457`: validation requires a non-empty string but does not parse or restrict URL schemes/origins.
* `crates/thegn-host/src/hydrate_calendar.rs:125-215`: periodic synchronization repeatedly rebuilds the router and its per-request clients.

## Required design

Centralize remote-calendar transport in a reusable, policy-configured client. Parse URLs at validation/startup. Disable automatic redirects or implement a small explicit redirect state machine that authenticates every hop: no origin change, no downgrade, no private/special-address pivot beyond an explicitly configured destination policy, no credential/body replay, bounded hop count, and DNS/address checks consistent across connect and redirect.

Read decoded bodies incrementally with a hard byte ceiling before allocation growth. Bound error bodies too. Apply connect, per-read/idle, and end-to-end deadlines; validate expected content types with documented compatibility exceptions. Reuse connection pools without allowing auth/state to bleed between accounts.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] HTTP(S)/webcal URLs are parsed and validated; unsupported schemes fail configuration validation.
- [ ] Redirects cannot change origin, downgrade confidentiality, pivot to an unapproved address class, or replay Authorization, cookies, URL credentials, or CalDAV sync-token bodies.
- [ ] 301/302/303/307/308, relative/absolute locations, loops, DNS rebinding, IPv4/IPv6 literals, and proxy configurations have adversarial tests.
- [ ] Decoded success and error bodies stop at the configured hard cap while streaming, independent of Content-Length and transfer/content encoding.
- [ ] Connect, idle/read, and total operation deadlines are distinct and tested with never-ending bodies.
- [ ] ICS and DAV media types are validated without rejecting documented real-world variants.
- [ ] A reusable client/pool is shared safely across polls and accounts; secrets cannot bleed through default headers.
- [ ] Logs and errors never contain subscription URLs, credentials, sync tokens, response bodies, or redirect locations with secrets.
- [ ] Resource-bound tests prove bounded memory under chunked/compressed oversized responses.

## Dependency mapping

This is calendar-specific application of the safe-HTTP work tracked in <issue id="d9997311-b5e1-4d21-9657-63f77178c15e" href="https://linear.app/blakeashley/issue/THE-321/centralize-safe-http-policy-for-authenticated-tracker-providers">THE-321</issue> (provider policy), <issue id="3af215de-c355-4aa7-b0ff-ca69e4e926df" href="https://linear.app/blakeashley/issue/THE-280/disable-authenticated-control-command-redirects-and-body-replay">THE-280</issue> (redirect/body replay), and <issue id="a1743b7e-904b-47e2-851f-14b563027a2e" href="https://linear.app/blakeashley/issue/THE-273/bound-control-client-deadlines-and-response-bodies-across-all">THE-273</issue> (deadlines/body limits). Coordinate on one shared transport primitive instead of adding another ad hoc client. It can land independently of <issue id="37123fdd-5d17-41e6-a3d7-822c165d706f" href="https://linear.app/blakeashley/issue/THE-450/separate-calendar-resource-series-and-recurrence-instance-identity">THE-450</issue> through <issue id="daedc829-ba25-450a-9317-97dde1cf6e04" href="https://linear.app/blakeashley/issue/THE-453/parse-caldav-multistatus-structurally-and-fail-closed">THE-453</issue> and should precede calendar fetch concurrency work.
